title: docs(changeset): the two pending console changesets count and mark all ten declared-breaking entries each (deliberate correction)
body:
Fixes #23136
Clause-②: no (published changelog text; no accept set or public surface widens)

## What this does

Two pending `@objectstack/console` changesets get corrected in place: `.changeset/console-20c6d351ad74.md` and `.changeset/console-f0268ad78485.md`. In each one:

- the count line reads 10 (it read 6 and 4);
- the entries the old digest left unmarked carry the uniform `**BREAKING**` marker: 4 in the first file, 6 in the second, 10 in all.

Both files are unconsumed. `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, `tag: next`, with 0 consumed changesets, read on `origin/main` `dc93781c1`. So whatever they say when the Version Packages PR merges ships in `@objectstack/console`'s CHANGELOG.

The 12 replaced lines are the digest's own output, copied line for line. `scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs` on `main` (the digest as of PR #23131) was re-run over each file's objectui range into a scratch file. I diffed that output against the committed file: it differs on exactly these 12 lines and on the ADR-0087 disposition comment, and nowhere else. The disposition comment was answered by hand, and the digest emits only its `TODO` placeholder there. So the comment stays as committed and the bump is not re-run.

The diff has no new changeset, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no `content/docs/releases/`, no `.changeset/pre.json` and no code: +12 / -12 over 2 files. I measured every edited file at base `dc93781c1` and head `6447f32ec` with an md5 of the extracted lines. The frontmatter bump block and the ADR-0087 disposition comment are byte-identical, and there is still exactly one `adr-0087:` marker per file:

| file | ADR-0087 comment, md5 (base = head) | frontmatter, md5 (base = head) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `console-20c6d351ad74.md` (lines 49-90, 42 lines) | `4d8165bda53cc2211ebc873b21a0dc8a` | `7f9512041627f495063dfc6b2bea2dc2` |
| `console-f0268ad78485.md` (lines 120-152, 33 lines) | `e503fdd7341c8ee1378fe8214dd7afbd` | `7f9512041627f495063dfc6b2bea2dc2` |

Neither file carries a `Clause-②` line, at base or at head. A raw-control-byte scan of both files finds nothing.

## The measurement, re-run on `main`

The objectui input is a full, non-shallow clone of `objectstack-ai/objectui` (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` answers `false`). All four endpoints resolve to commits. The shared sibling checkout is shallow and does not hold `20c6d351ad74` or `a58626c88dc8`, so it was not used.

```
node scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs --from 47b1f0bb7174 --to 20c6d351ad74 --objectui-root OBJECTUI_CLONE --out SCRATCH/digest-20c6.md
  exit 0, bump minor
  → 33 releasing changeset(s), 10 breaking (0 declared major, 10 annotated), 0 release-nothing, 1 commit(s) without a changeset

node scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs --from a58626c88dc8 --to f0268ad78485 --objectui-root OBJECTUI_CLONE --out SCRATCH/digest-f026.md
  exit 0, bump minor
  → 173 releasing changeset(s), 10 breaking (0 declared major, 10 annotated), 2 release-nothing, 4 commit(s) without a changeset
  → 1 of 175 changeset(s) added in this range no longer exist at f0268ad78485 … the account above is complete.
```

Both counts match the card (10 and 10), so no count differs from it.

**Control: the producer of the under-count.** I ran the digest as it stood before the two repairs, over the same ranges and the same clone. The version at `c9b5b24b0` (before PR #23131) and the one at `46064dfa0` (before PR #23117) both read `33 releasing, 6 breaking` and `173 releasing, 4 breaking`. The `46064dfa0` output equals both base files byte for byte outside the disposition comment. So the base text is that digest's output, and PR #23131 is the change that moves these two counts. PR #23117's decorated-opener reading moves neither of them.

## `check-empty-changeset` is red on purpose: DELIBERATE CORRECTION

`scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` refuses a diff that modifies a changeset present on the merge base (the foreign changeset rule). It names two classes with opposite remedies:

- COLLISION: restore theirs, rename yours.
- DELIBERATE CORRECTION: "do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed; restoring it from the base would put the false sentence back".

This PR is the second class by design, for both files. Each is a pending release note whose count line and markers under-state the breaking entries its own range declares. Nothing here is restored to turn the gate green. The gate stays red until the correction is confirmed. The direction on #23136 names that confirmation: a contract-tier review of record on this same head, as for #22586. That review names each changed note and judges each rewritten line, and the table below lists all 12.

The gate's output on head `6447f32ec` (`node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`, exit 1):

```
✓ No empty-frontmatter changeset introduced by this diff (2 declaring changeset(s) added).
This PR changes a changeset it did not add:
   .changeset/console-20c6d351ad74.md
     present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR -- this is somebody else's release note
   .changeset/console-f0268ad78485.md
     present on the merge base and CHANGED by this PR -- this is somebody else's release note
::error file=.changeset/console-20c6d351ad74.md::… DELIBERATE CORRECTION -- your change may have made this PENDING release note false, and you rewrote it in the same stroke. Remedy: do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed; …
::error file=.changeset/console-f0268ad78485.md::… (the same text)
```

## Scope statement: the disposition narratives now count fewer than the list (not changed here)

The direction on #23136 holds the ADR-0087 disposition comments byte-identical, and this PR keeps them that way. Their narrative sentences now name fewer breaking entries than the list above them:

- `console-20c6d351ad74.md:60-61` reads "The range carries six declared-breaking objectui changes, each by its author's breaking annotation and none by a declared `major`. Each is answered here:". It then answers (1) to (6). Lines 80-84 name three more by their `!` subjects: `3fd862510`, `025341692` and `c7b30bd66`. `8a55f0ccd` (row 1) is named nowhere in the comment.
- `console-f0268ad78485.md:130-131` reads "The range carries four declared-breaking objectui changes, each by its author's breaking annotation and none by a declared `major`. Each is answered here:". It answers (1) to (4). None of the six entries in rows 6 to 11 is named in the comment.
- Both comments close with the same sentence (`:88-89` and `:150-151`): "Scope of the claim, stated rather than implied: it is a claim about THIS diff, not a per-entry re-measurement of the upstream declared-breaking entries."

I checked whether any gate reads these sentences:

- **`check-adr-0087-registration` does not judge either file.** On this diff it prints "✓ check-adr-0087-registration: this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (2 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)." Both files declare breaking already at the merge base (`**BREAKING` in the body), and that gate exempts an `M` row that was breaking at base as inherited, before it reads any disposition. Its "non-breaking" wording covers those inherited rows as well.
- **It would not need per-entry answers if it did judge them.** I ran its own exported readers (`parseChangeset`, `breakingDeclaration`, `readDisposition`, `findMigrationPrescription`) on the head text of both files. Each reads `breaking=true`, disposition `not-required` / `no-migration-prescription`, and no migration prescription. The same holds at base. That category refuses only a body that carries a migration prescription. It does not read a count, and it does not require each breaking entry to be answered.
- **No script in the tree reads them.** `git grep` for "Each is answered" and "declared-breaking objectui changes" outside `.changeset/` hits only the released `packages/console/CHANGELOG.md`.

Every derived gate except the one above is green (Verification below), so no gate goes red on this tension.

What this leaves: the comment is an HTML comment. It renders as nothing, but it is copied verbatim into the raw `packages/console/CHANGELOG.md` text, the way earlier console comments already are there. So the stale "six" and "four" would ship in the raw CHANGELOG under the corrected count lines. Whether to route an update to these two comments is a call for the dispatching seat. This PR does not make it.

## Acceptance notes

- `check-adr-0087-registration` prints its count of skipped files as "non-breaking changeset(s) seen". Its `skipped` list holds both truly non-breaking files and files inherited as breaking from the base. On this diff both files are the second kind, so the line reads as if these two notes declared nothing breaking. This is an observation only. Nothing was filed.
- The ranges were re-measured in a scratch clone, and nothing was written into this repository other than the two files.
